title: Record the characteristic polynomial of one weight-3 c=3 joint space.
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->

## Change and mathematical scope

Proof and exhaustive evaluation on a named finite list, plus one named witness. No κ change. The selected conditional kappa stays `781451/250000000`.

For the historical 8-by-112 centre query, the joint eigenspace `(u, v) = (+1, -1)` inside weight-3 character 7 of sector `c=3` is 12-dimensional and `A_3`-invariant. Its monic characteristic polynomial is

```text
x^4 (x - 2)^4 (x + 2)^4.
```

On the pinned basis, `B = 4 A_3` is two 4-by-4 blocks of type `x^2 (x - 8)(x + 8)` and four scalar blocks `8, -8, -8, 8`. The block eigenvectors diagonalize `A_3` over `Q`. Eigenvalues `0`, `2` and `-2` each have geometric multiplicity 4.

The same polynomial is the characteristic polynomial on all twelve 12-dimensional joint spaces of the explicit pair `(u, v)`: the four weight-3 characters `7, 11, 13, 14`, and the three sign slots other than `(+1, +1)` on each. Each of those matrices of `B` is killed by `x(x - 8)(x + 8)`, so each space is diagonalizable over `Q` with the same multiplicities. One further pair, with an extra minus on coordinate 1, moves the 44-dimensional slot to `(-1, -1)` and still has this polynomial on its three 12-dimensional spaces. That pair is one witness, not a census of the cross-coset pairs.

The source first step names the `(+1, +1)` space of character 7. That space is 44-dimensional, so it is not the space in the question. The weight-4 polynomials `x^8 (x - 2)^4 (x + 2)^4` and `x^4 (x - 2)^2 (x + 2)^2` are different and were not recomputed. The factors `x`, `x - 8` and `x + 8` of `chi_B` divide all four published `c=3` sector polynomials. That comparison reads coefficients and does not replay the degree-881 certificate.

## Task and overlap

Base commit `17469fff78c22941280f04d39dc5a1faee09c840`. The live question is open-next item 2 of open PR #7021. Catalogue card `formal-interface-lemma`; scope status `changed`, because the card asks for a formal binding and this package answers the weight-3 polynomial left open by #7021.

Local overlap against that HEAD searched 10178 of 10178 note paths. No local note computes this polynomial. Targeted open-PR search found the question only as an open next step of #7021. Nearby open polynomials are the weight-4 `c=3` polynomial (#7021), the 8-dimensional and 48-dimensional `c=1` polynomials (#7019, #7036), and the `c=1` blocks in #7008, #7009 and #7023. None computes this 12-dimensional polynomial.

Not taken: the odd-sign factorisation of the weight-4 degree-16 polynomial, the payload-involution question, and the 216-dimensional, 48-dimensional and 8-dimensional `c=1` polynomials.

## Validation

Evidence class: a proof for the pinned basis and matrix, an exhaustive evaluation of the twelve named joint spaces, and one named witness. Not a heuristic search, and not a proof that every cross-coset pair has this polynomial.

```sh
python3 -B -W error research/c3-weight3-joint-charpoly/verify.py
python3 -B -O research/c3-weight3-joint-charpoly/verify.py
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/c3-weight3-joint-charpoly --check-only
```

Marker `PASS_C3_WEIGHT3_JOINT_CHARPOLY`. CPython 3.12, standard library. Both direct runs passed, about two seconds each, and the metadata check returned `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`. Selected-baseline orientation returned `PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY`.

Not run: Lean, Docker, the degree-881 replay, and the selected cold replay.

## Credit

The dimensions and the explicit pair come from #6965. The question is open-next item 2 of #7021. The query and the Bell action are retained from Ali Romman's PR4958 and PR4720. The sector coefficient lists are Krzysztof Wojt's exact one-slot package. The doubled representation comes from PR1719.

Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

Recorded in `research/c3-weight3-joint-charpoly/TASK.json`.

- Does every cross-coset pair have this same degree-12 polynomial on its 12-dimensional weight-3 joint spaces? The explicit pair and one coordinate-1 witness agree. This is not the weight-4 degree-16 splitting question.
- What is the characteristic polynomial of the 44-dimensional `(+1, +1)` joint space of character 7? The 12-dimensional calculation does not determine it.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

The source first step names the `(+1, +1)` space of character 7. For a weight-3 character that space has dimension 44, while the question asks for a 12-dimensional space. Naming the joint eigenvalues next to the dimension removes the ambiguity. https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1200
